To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

emergency medicine (EM) residents have positive attitudes toward electronic health records and electronic documentation and perceive that they improve workflow, and that EM residents' perceptions of the impact of EHRs on workflow are associated with their perceptions of the impact on patient care and on their work environment.
the EMR is perceived as an important tool for improving documentation, but that it also creates new challenges for workflow.

emergency medicine residents perceived that EHR use was associated with increased time spent documenting and decreased time spent on direct patient care, and that EHR use had negative effects on resident workflow, including interruptions to care.

the following questions.

the following: 1) the role that the emergency department plays in patient flow; 2) the impact of electronic medical record (EMR) on emergency physician documentation and patient flow; 3) the impact of EMR on the quality of care; 4) how EMR can be used to enhance emergency physician documentation and improve patient flow.
the development and implementation of an electronic documentation and workflow system (EDW) for emergency medicine resident physicians.

the use of EHR systems by emergency department physicians is a positive step in the right direction, as it has been shown to improve the overall workflow of the emergency department, and improve the efficiency in the documentation of patient care.
the use of EHRs in emergency medicine has both positive and negative effects on emergency physicians and their patients.

the use of electronic documentation in the emergency department (ED) is beneficial in terms of improving patient safety and quality of care and in terms of improving the workflow and efficiency of ED staff.

we found a high level of satisfaction with electronic medical records and the workflow that it has enabled.
the EMRs are not the cause of the problems in the emergency department, but they do exacerbate them.

emergency department documentation and workflow are perceived by residents as being inefficient, and that residents are willing to use a variety of strategies to improve efficiency.
there are a number of factors, both positive and negative, that influence the perception of EHRs and workflow.
